texts.preamble: Bd Lakshman Prasad Agarwal vs Union Of India & Ors on 28 May, 2015 Author: Arindam Sinha Bench: Arindam Sinha 1 17 28.05.15 W.P. 11164 (W) of 2015 akd & bd Lakshman Prasad Agarwal Vs. Union of India & Ors. -------- Mr. Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharyya, Mr. R. A. Agarwal, Mr. Kumar Gupta, Mr. Rajesh Gupta, Mrs. Nibedita Pal, Mr. Ramesh Dhara. ... For Petitioner Mr. Rudro Chatterjee ...
texts.facts: The consignment was put through Customs control, which by an examination order dated 18th May, 2015 recorded, inter alia, that assessment and examination has not been prescribed for the bill of entry while stating the compulsory compliance requirements to be fulfilled. The Government of India, Ministry of Agriculture, Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage by its order dated 19th May, 2015 recommended for release (for consumption purpose only) the consignment. The authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 by its communication dated 20th May, 2015 informed that the concerned bill of entry does not bear the complete name and address of the manufacturer, which is in violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.6 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011. According to them as it was a non rectifiable defect and sample was not drawn.
texts.arguments: Mr. Bhattacharyya, learned senior advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that his client is the packer and not the manufacturer. He further submits that wet dates cannot be manufactured. He relies on Section 27 of the said Act. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and the Customs Authorities are represented. They vehemently opposed any interim order being made regarding drawing of samples while the contentious issue of whether the importer is the manufacturer or a packer is deliberated upon. Bd Lakshman Prasad Agarwal vs Union Of India & Ors on 28 May, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116152613/ 1 Mr. Chatterjee, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 and 3 has relied upon a decision in the case of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India vs. Heartland Trading Company Pvt. Ltd. & Others reported in 2014 SCC OnLine Cal 19348 to draw attention of this Court to the following views expressed in that judgment. "It is not the law that if the imported food articles are found to be safe and wholesome for human consumption, then the Food Authority is bound to grant Heartland NOC, even if their labelling does not fulfil the requirements of the regulations.
